data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is a deterministic replay barrier combined with an exhaustive oracle-boundary audit log; it must durably record the replay barrier state and a total-ordered log of all non-deterministic inputs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The oracle audit log is incomplete due to implicit non-determinism such as interrupt timing or memory layout variations.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Replay cost from the barrier exceeds operational time bounds, making recomputation infeasible.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The workspace depends on external state that changed between the original computation and replay.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Since the workspace is deterministic per-problem, completed evidence is theoretically reproducible. The danger of silent displacement arises only if the workspace ingested non-reproducible oracle inputs (wall-clock time, hardware randomness, external sensory data). The protocol durably records a deterministic replay barrier (the exact problem input state) plus an exhaustive audit log of all oracle interactions. Reclamation rebuilds the workspace by replaying from the barrier using the audit log. Evidence is never displaced because it is either still present or exactly reproducible. This collapses the safety guarantee to completeness of the oracle log.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
